gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 13 build now compiles both the landed libfs starter tests and the new reviewability gate so the helper lane stays honest as it grows.
The existing make target keeps the bounded libfs starter and reviewability checks runnable through the same repeatable path as the other Zigux tranche checkpoints.

The landed starter already mirrors the pure helper-facing shape of simple_statfs(), always_delete_dentry(), and simple_lookup() without claiming live dcache mutation, inode locking, or VFS registration.

Dedicated starter tests keep the current wrapper honest around split fsid packing, default statfs values, negative-dentry discard intent, casefold passthrough, buffer-copy accounting, seek-policy bounds, directory-close release bookkeeping, directory-open private-data handoff, directory-emit handoff bookkeeping, and addressability planning.
The slice note records the narrow boundary of the landed helper lab so the lane does not overstate itself as live libfs or VFS parity.
A dedicated reviewability gate ties the current starter, tests, survey note, and roadmap traceability note together so future runs can confirm the lane state before widening helper coverage.
The survey note now describes the landed helper slice truthfully and keeps the remaining deeper VFS-state gaps explicit after the addressability helper landed.

The libfs helper lab now models the early seek-policy surface from dcache_dir_lseek() and offset_dir_llseek() in pure planning form, including SEEK_SET and SEEK_CUR handling, negative-offset rejection, max-position bounds, and whether a positive-entry scan would become necessary.

The libfs helper lab now adds one tiny dcache_readdir()-adjacent emit planner that models the dir_emit_dots() handoff, the transition into positive entry scanning, emitted-entry position accounting, and the early stop case before any live cursor dentries or inode-backed state are touched.

The libfs helper lab now models a bounded simple_transaction_get()/simple_transaction_set() staging-buffer planner around request-size bounds, one-write-per-open reservation, copy-fault retention, and publish-size bookkeeping without claiming live file-private storage or pseudo-filesystem plumbing.

The libfs helper lab now adds one tiny simple_transaction_read()/simple_transaction_release() follow-up that keeps the work in pure private-data presence checks, read delegation intent, and release bookkeeping without claiming live dentries, inode state, or pseudo-filesystem plumbing.

The libfs helper lab now models the smallest non-live dcache_dir_open() / dcache_readdir() cursor preconditions in planning form around cursor allocation failure, dir_emit_dots() gating, first-child-versus-cursor resume selection, and missing private-data blocking before any cursor dentries, sibling traversal, or lock ordering behavior is claimed.

The landed libfs helper lab now models the post-scan cursor reposition bookkeeping around hlist_del_init() plus hlist_add_before() / hlist_add_behind() in pure planning form, and the exported descriptor now reports that cursor-reposition planning explicitly so the review packet no longer hides an already-landed helper surface behind older starter scaffolding.

The libfs helper lab now models the tiny dcache_dir_close() release bookkeeping around dput(file->private_data) and the zero-error close outcome without claiming live refcount mutation, inode ownership, or directory teardown.

The libfs helper lab now models the tiny simple_open() private-data handoff in pure planning form so Zigux can keep the inode->i_private to file->private_data borrow explicit without claiming live inode mutation, open-time allocation, or broader file lifecycle ownership.

The libfs helper lab now models generic_check_addressable() in pure planning form around block-size validation, last-block accounting, sector-index overflow, page-index overflow, and empty-filesystem handling without claiming live superblock, page-cache, or inode ownership.
The remaining cursor-backed helpers still depend on live sibling traversal, reschedule-aware scans, lock ordering, and shared VFS object ownership that this helper lab should not claim yet.
Pseudo-filesystem setup, inode lifecycle helpers, rename-state behavior, and broader teardown paths still depend on live VFS state and ownership that stay outside this bounded Phase 13 helper slice.
